summary: The EmailPopupDocument module manages email attachment document records for a popup interface, including searching and deleting documents based on serialized string data.
purpose: To represent and control the lifecycle of documents attached to an email popup, allowing listing and deletion of files and associated folders.

fields.name: ID
fields.description: Unique identifier (sequential index) for the document

fields.name: FilePath
fields.description: Local server path to the file

fields.name: Checked
fields.description: Indicates if the document is selected/checked

workflows.name: Search for Email Popup Documents
steps: Receive serialized DataInfo string containing document metadata, separated by '|' delimiters.
For each entry, split by '>' into [filename, filepath].
If well-formed, instantiate EmailPopupDocument with sequential ID, filename, filepath.

workflows.name: Delete Email Popup Document
steps: Receive DataInfo string and target ID.
Iterate over DataInfo entries; for the matching ID:
Split out [filename, filepath], extract folder name from filepath.
Attempt to delete file at the given path.
Attempt to delete the associated folder.
Suppress and ignore any exceptions during file/folder deletion.
Reconstruct DataInfo string excluding the deleted entry.

business_rules: Only entries with exactly two parts separated by '>' are processed as valid documents.
IDs are assigned sequentially during Search execution.
File and folder deletion attempts are wrapped in try/catch; failures are suppressed (not surfaced to the caller).
validations: DataInfo must not be null or empty.
Entries must contain exactly one '>' delimiter separating filename and filepath.
calculations: ID is incremented sequentially for each parsed document in Search.
conditions: If DataInfo is empty, return an empty list or string.
system_behavior: Suppress exceptions when deleting files or folders (silent failure).
Document and folder deletions are performed on the file system based on parsed DataInfo.
dependencies: String parsing to manage document data
exceptions: Any exceptions during File.Delete or Directory.Delete are caught and ignored.
content_gaps: User interaction (UI) details are not described.
No information about handling permissions or security context for file deletion.
No information about persistence beyond in-memory string or the database field sources.
